reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and extends the existing weekend adjustment helper, although consumers still assemble the scheduling policy separately.

duplication.why: Daily exclusion and conditional date adjustment are repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Most policy lives in shared/schedules.ts, but the holiday-dependent shift bound remains in the server handler module.

scope.why: The edits focus on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting metadata and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: Shared holiday recognition is clear, but maintaining the complete skip-or-shift policy requires coordinating several independently composed paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Consumers use the existing recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment abstractions; getNextDate does not provide the enumeration interface needed by the range handler.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate expresses daily exclusion through find, while server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange express the same policy through filter followed by conditional adjustment.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter, and getNextDate gains a daily-specific filtering path; consumers reuse these helpers but duplicate their policy composition.
